I almost quit Karate after 8 years.

I started learning Karate when I was around 10 years old.

For years, every Tuesday and Thursday, I'd show up to training. I went from a white belt, all the way to brown.

But somewhere along the way, I started losing interest.

As I got older, Karate just didn't feel as exciting anymore. I wanted to stop.

But my parents encouraged me to keep going.

And I remember thinking:

"If I stop now, what do I have to show for all these years?"

So I kept going.

For another year and a half, I pushed through. I eventually switched to a much more intensive training session once a week and started putting in more effort than I had before.

After around 10 years of training, I finally earned my Black Belt. 🥋

Looking back, getting the Black Belt wasn't the hardest part.

The hardest part was continuing when I didn't want to.

Karate taught me something I've found myself using in almost everything I do now:

Motivation gets you started. Commitment keeps you going.

Sometimes you don't need to love what you're doing every day.

You just need to keep showing up.

You don't need to know how you're going to achieve your goal. You just need to believe it's possible.

I've started to realize this more and more over the years.

Before starting my clothing brands, I knew almost nothing about running a business.

I didn't know how to find manufacturers. I didn't know how to source products. I didn't know how to build a brand.

I just had an idea and wanted to see if I could make it work.

When we started working on STRAYED, I didn't even know how I was going to build the website from scratch with the limitations we had.

So I figured it out.

With Prettiva & Co., we initially tried Amazon because it seemed like the easiest way to get started. Eventually, we realized it wasn't the right fit for what we wanted to do.

So we looked for other options.

We tried things, changed our approach, found solutions that worked for us, and kept moving.

And that's probably one of the biggest things I've learned from all of this:

You don't always need the answer before you start.

Sometimes you just need a goal big enough that you're willing to figure out the rest along the way.

There will be things you don't know.
There will be things that don't work.
There will be times when you have no idea what to do next.

But there's almost always another way forward.

It might take weeks. It might take months.

But if you keep looking, keep learning, and don't give up, you'll eventually find a way.

So dream big.

Don't limit your goals based on what you think is possible today.

Set the goal first.

Figure out the how along the way.
